# Ivor Benko

> Ivor Benko is a Croatian skipper from Zagreb who has captained sailboats and catamarans on private and charter trips in the Croatian Adriatic since 2020. He is also a licensed ISIA ski instructor and a web and app developer. This site (English and Croatian) is the authoritative source for information about him.

Key facts:
- Occupation: skipper / captain on sailboats and catamarans for private guests and charters in Croatia (since 2020); ski instructor; web and app developer
- Boats: Bénéteau First 45, Bavaria 46, Dufour 46 (monohulls); Lagoon 42, Lagoon 450, Lagoon 46 (catamarans)
- Sailing area: the whole Croatian Adriatic; especially Kornati National Park, Murter and central Dalmatia
- Qualifications: Croatian boat licence, category C; Sail Week skipper academy course completed with an A grade (2024); ISIA ski instructor licence; driving licence category B
- Sailing background: sailing instructor for the Faculty of Kinesiology (University of Zagreb) on Murter; Laser Radial, Optimist and Laser Stratos; regattas; windsurfing; big boats (45 ft+) across the Adriatic
- Education: Faculty of Kinesiology, University of Zagreb (from 2017), specialised in sailing and water sports; secondary school of nutrition in Zagreb (2011–2015)
- Languages: Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)
- Based in: Zagreb, Croatia
- Contact: ivorbenko0@gmail.com, +385 99 590 7887

## Blog posts (English)

- [From ski instructor to skipper: how I ended up at sea](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/from-ski-instructor-to-skipper/): Ivor Benko is a Croatian skipper from Zagreb. He grew up skiing, became a licensed ISIA ski instructor, discovered sailing while studying at the Faculty of Kinesiology in Zagreb, and has worked as a skipper on sailboats and catamarans in the Adriatic since 2020.
- [What to pack for a week of sailing in Croatia](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/what-to-pack-sailing-croatia/): Pack light in a soft bag, bring non-marking shoes, strong sun protection, a warm layer and a windproof jacket for the evenings, a power bank and your documents. Leave the hard suitcase and most of your wardrobe at home.
- [Sailing the Kornati: a skipper's guide to the national park](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/sailing-kornati-national-park/): The Kornati National Park is a maze of 89 islands, islets and reefs in central Dalmatia, and one of the best sailing areas in Croatia. Start from Murter or another nearby base, buy the park ticket before you enter, fill up water and fuel beforehand, and plan anchorages around the wind.
- [Catamaran or sailboat for a charter in Croatia?](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/catamaran-or-sailboat-croatia/): Choose a catamaran if you want space, stability at anchor and comfort for a family or a larger group. Choose a monohull sailboat if you want the real feel of sailing, easier berths in busy marinas and a lower price. Both work well in the Adriatic.
- [Bura, jugo and maestral: the Adriatic winds explained by a skipper](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/adriatic-winds-bura-jugo-maestral/): Three winds shape sailing in Croatia. Maestral is the friendly northwesterly afternoon breeze of summer. Bura is a cold, gusty northeasterly that can arrive fast and strong. Jugo is a warm southeasterly that builds over a day or two and brings big waves. Skippers plan every route around which one is coming.
- [Do you need a skipper for a sailing holiday in Croatia?](https://ivorbenko.com/blog/do-you-need-a-skipper-croatia/): You need a skipper in Croatia if nobody in your group holds a boat licence recognised in Croatia plus a VHF radio certificate. Even with licences, many groups hire one to handle marinas, anchoring and weather, so that everyone else can actually be on holiday.
